readme.title: What this module covers
readme.html:
What this module covers

This module explains how AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI nest inside each other, and which AWS services fill each of the three tiers in the AWS AI/ML stack. It then turns to data analytics, covering data lakes, ETL and the AWS services behind each phase of an automated data pipeline. A closing real-life example joins both halves with an e-commerce pipeline that lets data scientists query, and ML engineers retrain on, the same S3 dataset.

readme.title: Lessons
readme.html:
Lessons

Module 8 Introduction

  1. Introduction to AI and Machine Learning: AI versus ML versus classical programming, plus training and inference, told through the coffee shop.

AI/ML on AWS

  1. AI/ML on AWS: common ML business uses and the AWS AI/ML stack's three tiers.
  2. AWS AI/ML Solutions: a comparison table of the pre-built AI services, then Amazon SageMaker AI and ML frameworks and infrastructure.
  3. Introduction to Generative AI on AWS: deep learning, foundation models, LLMs and the AWS generative AI lineup.
  4. AWS Generative AI Solutions: SageMaker JumpStart, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Q Business and Amazon Q Developer side by side.

Data Analytics on AWS

  1. Introduction to Data Analytics: data analytics, data lakes, ETL, ELT, zero-ETL and data pipelines.
  2. Data Pipelines on AWS: a phase-by-phase table of AWS pipeline services and how to tell look-alikes apart.

Cloud in Real Life

  1. Data Analytics and AI/ML: an eight-step e-commerce pipeline that feeds one S3 dataset to Athena queries and SageMaker AI retraining.

readme.title: Key takeaways
readme.html:
Key takeaways

  • A hand-written rule is classical programming, while ML learns patterns from history, packages them in a model and applies that model to new data (inference).
  • The assessment feedback adds that ML usually demands more compute than classical programming, and that classical code still powers complex systems such as operating systems.
  • Deep learning trains layered neural networks, and generative AI is deep learning built on foundation models, which are trained once on huge datasets and then reused for many jobs.
  • The AWS AI/ML stack runs from pre-built AI services, through ML services centered on Amazon SageMaker AI (your own models, AWS-run infrastructure), to ML frameworks and infrastructure (full control, infrastructure you manage).
  • Match the AI service to the job: Comprehend for sentiment and key phrases, Polly to speak text, Transcribe to write speech, Translate for languages, Kendra for enterprise search, Rekognition for images and video, Textract for document text, Lex for chat and voice bots, Personalize for recommendations.
  • For generative AI, SageMaker JumpStart is a hub of ready models, Amazon Bedrock serves many FMs through one API with standard pay-as-you-go pricing, Amazon Q Business helps employees with company data, and Amazon Q Developer suggests code.
  • Data analytics mines historical data for insights and stays relevant next to AI/ML, for example when a lender must explain a decision.
  • Pipelines automate ETL so the same steps run reliably every time, with less manual effort.
  • In a pipeline, Kinesis Data Streams and Data Firehose ingest, S3 (data lake) and Redshift (data warehouse) store, Glue Data Catalog catalogs, Glue and EMR process, Athena and Redshift query, and QuickSight and OpenSearch Service visualize.
  • One automated pipeline can serve both analytics and ML training from the same S3 dataset.

The module assessment has 10 questions.

  • Classical programming versus machine learning: 1 question.

  • Amazon SageMaker AI as the way to build custom models without managing infrastructure: 1 question.
  • What defines foundation models: 1 question.
  • How Amazon Bedrock exposes foundation models: 1 question.
  • Choosing a generative AI assistant that works from company data (Amazon Q Business): 1 question.
  • What data pipelines add to ETL: 1 question.
  • Real-time data ingestion with Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: 1 question.
  • Which services serve as data lake and data warehouse: 1 question.
  • Several questions lean on look-alike services as distractors, so know where Amazon Comprehend, Amazon EMR and Amazon Athena fit (3, 3 and 2 questions respectively).

readme.title: Summary
readme.html:
Summary

Good data feeds two kinds of work: AI/ML points it at the future, while analytics points it at the past. On the AI/ML side, the module covered AWS services that forecast what comes next and automate processes. On the analytics side, it covered AWS services that collect, prepare and explore historical data so people can learn from it.

Introduction to AI and Machine Learning

Objectives

Notes

Why data comes first

  • AI/ML forecasts and automates, while mines history for insight.
  • Shop data (visitors, rush hours, best sellers) could guide bean orders, new sites and drinks, if collected cleanly.

AI, ML and classical programming

  • AI: the broad field of computer systems that do humanlike tasks.
  • ML: AI where machines learn complex jobs from data, not spelled-out instructions.
  • hard-codes a rule from past pairings (a cheese Danish with every caramel latte), ignoring the individual customer and product.

Training and inference

  • : ML finds hidden customer-sales patterns in lots of history and outputs a model.
  • : the model gets new data, like a fresh order, and predicts or decides.
  • Result: suggestions fitted to each customer's order history, and more food sold.

Conversational and predictive AI

  • A counter kiosk could take spoken orders, enter them in the register for baristas and use to offer an extra shot or the new seasonal latte.
  • Being , not rule-based, it adapts to answers in real time.
  • Another AI could mix local social trends with sales history to forecast hits or propose recipes.

AI/ML on AWS

  • With you create, train and deploy custom models, while AI services offer pre-built ones (translation, image recognition).
  • On demand, they spare businesses of any size the time and cost of building from scratch.
  • Training data (sales, social posts, sensors, feedback forms) must be gathered, cleaned and formatted first.

Key takeaways

  • Training builds a model from history, and inference applies it to new data.
  • A fixed pairing rule is classical programming, while per-customer suggestions come from ML.
  • ML is only as accurate as its data.

Scenarios

  • Pastry suggestions from each customer's history: an ML recommendation engine, a headline ML use case.
  • A kiosk taking spoken orders: conversational AI with NLP.

Terms

  • Artificial intelligence (AI): Computer systems performing humanlike tasks.
  • Machine learning (ML): AI that learns from data patterns, not written instructions.
  • Classical programming: Hand-coding fixed rules instead of learning them.
  • Training: Finding patterns in historical data to build a model.
  • Inference: Applying a trained model to new data.
  • Natural language processing (NLP): What lets the course's kiosk grasp speech and ask follow-ups.
  • Conversational AI: AI that adapts to replies, unlike rule-based systems.

AI/ML on AWS

Objectives

  • Spot common AI/ML business uses.

Notes

Use cases

  • Amazon uses ML for recommendations and fulfillment.
  • ML predicts (stock trends, prices of goods), decides (routing a caller by spoken request) and detects anomalies (online-banking fraud).

The three tiers

  • AI services: managed, pre-trained models for set jobs, such as (text to speech) and (text and sentiment).
  • ML services: for more customization, you create, train and ship custom models in while AWS manages infrastructure, tools and workflows, with experiments, data visuals, debugging and monitoring in one place.
  • ML frameworks and infrastructure: fully custom work for specialized needs, on purpose-built chips with popular frameworks or ML-optimized EC2.

Key takeaways

  • ML predicts, decides and detects anomalies.
  • Tiers run from ready-made (AI services) to your own models (SageMaker AI) to fully custom.
  • SageMaker AI is the main ML services example.

Terms

  • AWS AI/ML stack: AI services, ML services, and ML frameworks and infrastructure.
  • Amazon SageMaker AI: Fully managed service where you create custom ML models.

Deep learning

Generative AI

  • Deep learning producing original content and ideas (conversations, stories, images, music), powered by foundation models (FMs), huge models pre-trained on massive data.
  • One FM adapts to many tasks, while classic ML models do one.

  • Generative AI: Deep learning that creates new content.
  • Foundation model (FM): Huge pre-trained, multi-task model.

introduction-to-data-analytics.html:
Introduction to Data Analytics

Objectives

  • Explain the purpose and benefits of pipelines.
  • Define .

Notes

Analytics next to AI/ML

  • Data enables AI/ML, whose predictions reshape analysis.
  • Both need plenty of clean, easy-to-reach data.
  • Data analytics: analysts turn raw history into insights and trends.
  • Still vital: explaining loan decisions, hypothesis tests on clinical trials, insurance risk models regulators can understand and approve, and cheaper, more efficient work on small datasets.

Data lakes

  • Purchases, logins and browsing leave data scattered across systems and formats, and a , pictured as a huge reservoir, gathers it all.

ETL, ELT and zero-ETL

  • Data must also suit analytics tools and AI algorithms.
  • ETL: extract and store, transform to one format, load into a warehouse or analytics platform.
  • : load first, transform as needed; needs and infrastructure decide.
  • : skip it when data is already usable and in place.

Pipelines and AWS

  • Pipelines are assembly lines automating ingest, process and serve, so each ETL run repeats reliably.
  • Named here: Amazon Kinesis and (ingest), and Redshift (store), (process), (visualize).
  • Lesson 7 moves Glue to cataloging and processing, leaving ingestion to Kinesis Data Streams and Firehose.
  • One S3 dataset can feed marketing's QuickSight BI and SageMaker AI training.

Key takeaways

  • Analytics still matters beside AI/ML.
  • A data lake centralizes scattered data.
  • ETL transforms before loading, ELT after, and zero-ETL not at all.
  • Pipelines make each ETL run consistent and hands-off.

Scenarios

  • Explaining a loan decision: traditional analytics.

Terms

  • Data analytics: Raw history turned into insights.
  • Data lake: One store for all of a business's data.
  • ETL: Extract, transform, load, which formats data before loading.
  • ELT: Extract, load, transform, which formats data after loading.
  • Zero-ETL: Using already-usable data as-is.
  • Data pipeline: Automated ingest-process-deliver line.

Data Pipelines on AWS

Objectives

  • Match AWS services to each phase of a typical .

Notes

What a pipeline does

  • It automates source-to-destination flow (ingest, catalog, transform, deliver) from apps, databases, sensors and streams, cutting manual work and errors.
  • Insight needs the data pooled in one place: a flexible for vast raw data, or a more structured built for business intelligence.
  • Ingestion moves source data into that store, in real time when needed at once, or in batches when delay is tolerable.
  • Cataloging records centrally as an inventory of the organization's data, much as a phone selfie carries its time, place and file format.
  • Processing then cleans and transforms the data, and consumers query and visualize it.

  • Athena queries data where it lives and bills per query, while Redshift handles frequent, heavy SQL.
  • QuickSight is for BI dashboards, while OpenSearch Service is for real-time search and monitoring.

Scenarios

  • Live stock data feeding instant trades: Kinesis Data Streams.
  • Gathering every smart home device's data for long-term analysis: Data Firehose.

data-analytics-and-ai-ml.html:
Data Analytics and AI/ML

Objectives

  • Explain how a company can automate ingesting, processing and delivering data.

Notes

The problem

  • An e-commerce app's recommendation model needs regular retraining on fresh customer data.
  • Its data scientists want to query that data too.
  • Nonstop collection and analysis suit an efficient, repeatable, error-free automated pipeline.
  • Customer history sits in , great for fast reads and writes but impractical to scan in full for training, so the data must move to a .

The pipeline, marker by marker

  • 1 Make recommendations: the ML model suggests products to shoppers.
  • 2 Store app data: DynamoDB keeps the customer history.
  • 3 Ingest data: with no direct DynamoDB-to-Firehose link today, changes go through , then Data Firehose aggregates them (near real time, little setup, auto scaling).
  • 4 Process data: records arrive as JSON, but the data scientist and ML engineer want .csv, so Firehose invokes an function to convert them.
  • 5 Deliver data: Firehose writes it to the S3 data lake, which holds all the company's ML and analytics data for many consumers.
  • 6 Catalog data: an table notes the data's schema and where it sits in S3, so ad hoc queries can find it.
  • 7 Perform : data scientists query S3 in place with standard in , which reads the catalog table to recognize the structure.
  • 8 Train model: pulls that same S3 data so ML engineers can retrain the recommendation model.

Why automate

  • Once built, the pipeline reruns on a schedule, so data scientists focus on insights and ML engineers on keeping the model current.
  • Reusing one dataset is common, and the course calls automation key to efficiency and innovation.

Visuals

  • Architecture diagram: the eight numbered markers above, ending in a split to Athena (analytics) and SageMaker AI (training) that shows one pipeline serving both.

Key takeaways

  • DynamoDB suits app reads and writes, not training scans, so data moves to an S3 data lake.
  • Kinesis Data Streams bridges DynamoDB to Firehose, which can call Lambda to reshape records before S3.
  • One scheduled pipeline feeds both Athena analysis and SageMaker AI training from the same S3 data.

Scenarios

  • A fresh model plus data scientists' queries on the same data: an automated pipeline.
  • Data arriving as JSON but needed as .csv: Firehose invoking a .

Terms

  • AWS Lambda: Runs functions; here Firehose invokes one to transform records before delivery (see AWS Lambda).

questions.stem: The cafe's analysts want to ask questions of the order files in its S3 data lake using standard SQL. They want to query the files right where they sit, without setting up or running a data warehouse. Which service fits?

options.why: Redshift is a data warehouse the cafe would have to set up and run, which the analysts want to avoid.
EMR runs big data processing clusters rather than serving quick SQL queries on files in place.
Athena runs standard SQL directly against the data where it sits in S3, with nothing to load first.
RDS hosts a relational database that would need the order data loaded into it before any query.

questions.stem: The cafe's app keeps its order history in Amazon DynamoDB and suggests pastries from a model that needs retraining on fresh orders. Its analysts also want to query that same order data. Which setup keeps both groups supplied with fresh orders, hands-off?

options.text: Point Athena and SageMaker AI at the DynamoDB table

options.text: Export the orders to S3 by hand when a group asks

labs.title: AI service per cafe task
labs.brief: The cafe has a list of jobs it wants AI to help with this season, but it has no data scientists and wants ready-made models. Sort each task under the pre-built AWS AI service that does it.

cards.text: A year of written reviews to tag as pleased, neutral or annoyed
Comments typed into the app's feedback box, checked for the phrases guests mention most
The day's specials spoken in a natural voice at the drive-through
An audio version of the barista training guide, made without a studio
The online menu shown in the language each visiting tourist reads
Letters from a bean supplier abroad turned into the staff's own language
A helper in the app that guests type or speak to and that answers about their order
A phone line where callers ask about opening hours and the system understands and replies
Drink suggestions for each loyalty member drawn from what they ordered before
A row on the order screen showing what is trending with customers this week

goals.label: Both feedback jobs sit under Amazon Comprehend
goals.hint: Ask whether the job pulls meaning, such as mood or key phrases, out of text that guests already wrote.

goals.label: Both spoken-word jobs sit under Amazon Polly
goals.hint: Ask whether written words must come out as lifelike speech, with nobody talking back.

goals.label: Both language jobs sit under Amazon Translate
goals.hint: Ask whether the words must end up in a different language from the one they arrived in.

goals.label: Both conversation jobs sit under Amazon Lex
goals.hint: Ask whether a guest holds a two-way exchange, by voice or text, that the system must understand before it replies.

goals.label: Both suggestion jobs sit under Amazon Personalize
goals.hint: Ask whether the result is a pick for the customer, drawn from the history of past orders.

lines: Pre-built AI services hand the cafe trained models for set jobs, so it can start fast without data scientists.
Comprehend pulls sentiment and key phrases out of text, while Translate turns that text into another language.
Polly only turns written text into lifelike speech, while Lex understands a guest's voice or text and holds the conversation.
Personalize draws on past orders to give each customer picks of their own.

questions.takeaway: A team with no ML skill that needs review sentiment fast fits a pre-trained AI service such as Comprehend.

read.text: Ready-made and fastest to deploy; later tiers add customization and need more skill.

questions.stem: The cafe has no data scientists, and it wants to start sorting customer reviews by mood next week. Which approach gets it there fastest?

options.why: SageMaker AI asks the team to build and train its own model, which needs ML skill the cafe lacks.
Comprehend comes pre-trained to read sentiment in text, so the cafe can sort reviews by mood with no ML staff.
Personalize is pre-trained too, but it makes per-customer picks rather than reading the mood of a review.
Polly is a ready-made service, but it turns text into speech and judges nothing about how a review feels.

questions.takeaway: Building a voice or text chat bot into an app points to Amazon Lex.

read.text: Lifelike voice or text chat via NLU and ASR (language understanding, speech recognition)

questions.stem: The cafe wants a bot in its ordering app that customers can type to or talk to, which understands what they ask for and replies. Which service builds that conversational interface?

options.why: Polly can give a bot a voice, but it does not understand what a customer types or says.
Q Business is an assistant that answers questions from company data, not a builder for customer chat bots.
Lex adds voice or text conversation to apps, using language understanding and speech recognition.
Comprehend analyzes stored text for insights and does not hold a two-way conversation with a customer.

questions.takeaway: Ready-made, per-customer recommendations from order history point to Amazon Personalize.

read.text: Per-customer picks from historical data

questions.stem: The cafe wants its loyalty app to suggest drinks to each member based on what they ordered before. It has no ML team and wants a ready-made service. Which service fits?

options.why: SageMaker AI could build such a model, but the cafe would have to create and train it, which needs ML skill.
Kendra answers search queries over company content rather than suggesting items to each customer.
Comprehend analyzes text for sentiment and key phrases and does not recommend products.
Personalize is a pre-built service that makes per-customer picks from past behavior with no ML team needed.

labs.title: Build the sales pipeline
labs.brief: Every till in the cafe sends each sale the moment it rings up, and the area managers, none of them developers, want sales dashboards they can build and read themselves. Place one service in each stage of the sales pipeline, and put any service with no job here on Not used. In this lab, each stage holds the service that does that stage's job, and the sales rows reach the lake in a shape the query tool can read, so no big data cluster is needed.

questions.takeaway: When several apps must read the same events the moment they happen, ingest them with Kinesis Data Streams.

read.text: Kinesis Data Streams is real time with many readers, while Firehose is near real time with managed delivery.

questions.stem: The cafe wants to take in kiosk orders as the first step of its data pipeline. A live stock board and a fraud analytics app must both read every order the moment it lands, with no lag. Which service should ingest the order data?

options.why: Kinesis Data Streams ingests data in real time and lets several apps, such as the stock board and the fraud check, read one stream at once.
Firehose delivers data in near real time to a destination, so it adds the small lag the cafe cannot accept.
A queue hands each message to one consumer for processing, rather than letting two readers see every order live.
Glue runs transform jobs on data already stored, so it cannot ingest orders for live reads at the moment they land.

questions.takeaway: Business intelligence dashboards that non-experts build themselves point to Amazon Quick Sight.

read.text: QuickSight is for BI dashboards, while OpenSearch Service is for real-time search and monitoring.

questions.stem: The cafe owner, who has no coding skills, wants interactive dashboards and reports of weekly sales by branch without running any servers. Which service fits?

options.why: OpenSearch Service targets real-time search and monitoring of operational data, not business intelligence reports.
Quick Sight lets non-experts build interactive business intelligence dashboards and reports with no infrastructure.
Athena runs SQL queries but does not give the owner dashboards or reports to share.
CloudWatch shows metrics about AWS resources and apps, not business reports on sales.

incidents.title: Reviews from the festival crowd
incidents.brief: After the summer food festival, the cafe's review page fills up with comments from visitors all over the world, and the manager wants to make sense of them before the next weekend.

steps.takeaway: Converting a large batch of written text into another language points to Amazon Translate.

read.text: Live or batch translation for global communication

steps.stem: A large pile of festival reviews is written in Spanish, Japanese and German, and the cafe manager reads only English. She wants every review turned into English in one overnight run. Which service fits?

options.why: Comprehend finds sentiment and key phrases in text, but it leaves each review in its original language.
Translate converts text from one language to another, and it can work through a large batch at once.
Transcribe turns spoken audio into text, and these reviews are already written down.
Polly reads text aloud as speech, which does not change the language the review is written in.

steps.takeaway: Pulling the key phrases out of large amounts of written feedback points to Amazon Comprehend.

read.text: NLP for key phrases, language, sentiment in documents

steps.stem: The cafe's festival reviews are all in English now. The manager wants each one tagged with the key phrases it mentions, such as a drink or a dish, so the most common topics stand out without anyone reading every review. Which service fits?

options.why: Kendra answers search questions over company content, and it does not tag each review with its phrases.
Textract pulls text out of scanned forms and documents, but these reviews are already plain text.
Comprehend uses NLP to pull the key phrases out of documents, so it can tag each review by topic.
Rekognition analyzes images and video, not the wording of written reviews.

steps.takeaway: Turning written scripts into natural speech in several languages points to Amazon Polly.

read.text: Text to lifelike speech; many languages, genders, accents

steps.stem: Several reviewers said the greeting on the cafe's phone line was hard to follow. The manager wants new spoken greetings in English, Spanish and German, made from scripts the staff already wrote in each language, without hiring voice actors. Which service fits?

options.why: Transcribe turns speech into text, the opposite of turning a written script into a spoken greeting.
Lex runs two-way conversations, while a fixed greeting only needs the script spoken aloud.
The scripts already exist in each language, and Translate does not turn text into speech.
Polly turns written text into lifelike speech in many languages, so no voice actors are needed.

incidents.title: Croissants in the bin
incidents.brief: Most evenings the cafe throws away trays of unsold croissants, and the owner has hired a data scientist to bring the morning bake closer to what really sells.

steps.takeaway: Estimating a future quantity, such as tomorrow's sales, is a prediction job for machine learning.

read.text: ML predicts (stock trends, prices of goods), decides (routing a caller by spoken request) and detects anomalies (online-banking fraud).

steps.stem: The cafe wants a model that works out from past sales how many croissants will sell tomorrow, so the bakers know how many to make. Which kind of machine learning job is this?

options.why: Anomaly detection flags unusual events, such as fraud, rather than estimating tomorrow's sales.
Routing sends a request, such as a phone call, to the right place, which is not estimating sales.
Estimating tomorrow's sales from past sales is a prediction, like forecasting the price of goods.
Creating original text or images is generative work, not estimating a sales figure.

steps.takeaway: Training turns historical data into a model, and using that model on new data comes afterward.

read.text: Training: ML finds hidden customer-sales patterns in lots of history and outputs a model.

steps.stem: A data scientist feeds the cafe's long sales history into an ML algorithm to find the patterns behind croissant demand. What does this training stage produce?

options.text: A fixed rule that a developer wrote
options.why: A hand-written rule is classical programming, while training learns the patterns from data.
A forecast for a new day comes later, once the finished model is run on fresh data.

options.text: A model of the sales patterns
options.why: Training finds the hidden patterns in historical data and outputs a model that captures them.

options.text: A cleaned copy of the sales records
options.why: Cleaning and formatting the data happens before training starts, not as its result.

steps.takeaway: Amazon SageMaker AI is one managed place to experiment with, debug and monitor your own ML models.

read.text: IDE: access control, visibility, experiments, data visualization, debugging, monitoring; plus hundreds of fast-deploy pre-trained models.

steps.stem: The cafe's data scientist wants one managed AWS environment where she can run experiments on her own forecasting model, visualize the data, debug the model and monitor it after deployment, without running any servers. Which service fits?

options.why: Personalize serves ready-made recommendations, and it is not a workspace for building and debugging her own model.
SageMaker AI gives one managed place to experiment with, debug and monitor her own model while AWS runs the servers.
Bedrock offers managed foundation models through an API, not a workspace for her own forecasting model.
Rekognition is a pre-trained image and video service with no place to build or monitor her own model.

steps.takeaway: Running a trained model on the day's fresh data to get a forecast is inference.

read.text: Inference: the model gets new data, like a fresh order, and predicts or decides.

steps.stem: Each morning the cafe's trained demand model receives that day's weather and weekday and returns how many croissants to bake. Which ML stage runs each morning?

options.why: Training already happened on the sales history, and the morning run only applies the finished model.
Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained model with more data, but this run uses the model as it is.
Gathering and cleaning data comes before training, not when the model makes its daily forecast.
Inference feeds new data to a trained model so it can predict, which is what happens each morning.

incidents.title: The autumn app feature
incidents.brief: The autumn menu launches soon, and the cafe's only programmer has been asked to add a feature to the ordering app that describes each new drink to customers before release day.

steps.takeaway: Building a secure production app on managed foundation models points to Amazon Bedrock.

read.text: Managed FMs from Amazon and startups (Claude, Stable Diffusion) via one API; test, tune, integrate

steps.stem: The cafe's developer wants the ordering app to call a foundation model that writes drink descriptions for customers. She wants a secure, private service built for production apps, with AWS managing the models. Which service fits?

options.why: Q Business is an assistant for the cafe's staff, not a model service to build into a customer app.
Personalize recommends items from past activity, and it does not write new descriptions.
Bedrock offers managed foundation models through one API for secure, private production apps.
Lex builds chat interfaces that understand requests, but it does not supply models that write text.

steps.takeaway: A model that creates more than one type of content, such as text and images, is multimodal.

read.text: Multimodal: Generating several content types.

steps.stem: A feature in the cafe's app uses a generative AI model to write drink descriptions. Marketing wants that one model to also create a matching picture of each drink. What kind of model does the feature need?

options.why: Fine-tuning adapts a model with the cafe's own data, but it does not add the ability to make images.
A multimodal model generates several content types, so one model can return both text and images.
An LLM is trained on text for human language, so it writes descriptions but does not draw pictures.
A classic ML model handles one narrow job, such as a forecast, and does not create images.

steps.takeaway: A coding assistant in the IDE that helps with security and code reviews points to Amazon Q Developer.

read.text: Suggests code, even whole functions and logical blocks, in multiple IDEs; languages include C#, Java, JavaScript, Python, TypeScript

steps.stem: Before release day, the programmer who builds the cafe's app wants an assistant inside her code editor that reviews her Python code for security problems and suggests fixes. Which service fits?

options.why: JumpStart is a hub of models to fine-tune and deploy, not an assistant that reviews code.
Q Business answers staff questions from company repositories, and it is not a coding assistant.
Bedrock offers foundation models to build apps with, not a ready assistant inside her editor.
Q Developer works inside IDEs, suggesting code and helping with security and code reviews.
